assumptions: New authored crank-rocker consumer, not an ARX or IRIS design revision
One supplier-independent DC torque-port model drives the crank; its reaction housing and output shaft are shown, electromagnetic internals are not modeled
All moving mass and full inertia come from the generated nominal steel CAD without mass overrides
The integral steel load lobe is on the passive rocker; gravity supplies its load and the single coupler supplies the driving constraint force
Ideal revolute bearings and a connect closure represent pin constraints; local bearing contact, elasticity, wear and friction qualification are absent
Mating clearances and retainer grooves are nominal CAD; supplier fits, production tolerance stack and retention strength require measured process data and hardware testing
Motor constants, damping and material densities are explicit engineering assumptions, not measured hardware data
Native sampled interference results do not prove continuous-time clearance or hardware load capacity
